expression:
local({
  child <- as.numeric(m133)
  parents <- cbind(as.numeric(m134), as.numeric(m135))
  native_parent <- rowSums(parents == 1, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
  known <- rowSums(!is.na(parents)) > 0
  case_when(
    native_parent ~ "Native",
    known & child == 1 ~ "Second-generation",
    known & child %in% 2:6 ~ "First-generation",
    .default = "Unknown"
  )
})
notes: 2014 only, optional item: country of birth of the student, mother and father (resident country or abroad). Native if either parent was born in the country, otherwise generation by the student's birthplace; where one parent is missing the other decides.

notes: Derived from the who-lives-in-main-home tick list (1=Yes, 2=No; 0 is a 2001 missing code). Two biological/adoptive parents = mother and father both in the main home (the rare household ticking mother, father and a step-parent is classified here, first branch wins); Step family = at least one of mother/father plus at least one step-parent; Single parent = exactly one of mother/father and no step-parent (a parent's cohabiting partner is only detectable if the child reported them as a step-parent); Other = roster answered but no biological/adoptive parent in the main home (grandparents, foster/children's home, and rare step-parent-only households); Unknown = all four parental items missing. Classified on the main home only: second-home items (havehome2/timehome2) are inconsistently collected and not used, so shared-care arrangements are classified by their main home.
